memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After forty days Noah opened a window he had made in the ark and sent out a raven, and it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth. Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had receded from the surface of the ground. - Gen 8:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even after the ark rested, Noah did not simply fling open the door and rush out. He waited, and he tested - first sending a raven, then a dove - patiently discerning whether the time was right. Here is a man who had trusted God to bring him through the flood, now trusting God's timing to bring him out of the ark.

There is real wisdom in Noah's patience. It would have been tempting, after so long cooped up, to hurry out at the first sign of dry land. But Noah waited on God rather than rushing ahead of Him. He had learned that God's deliverance comes not only in the right way but at the right time.

We often struggle here. We trust God for the big rescue but grow impatient with His timing for the next step. We want to fling open the door and move before God says "go." Yet some of the costliest mistakes in life come from good desires acted on too soon, running ahead of the Lord.

The Bible calls us to "wait for the Lord" and to "be strong and take heart" while we wait (Ps 27:14). Waiting is not wasted time; it is trust in action. Like Noah watching the dove, we learn to move at God's pace, not our own. The God who is faithful to save is also faithful in His timing - and His timing is always worth waiting for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you tempted to rush ahead of God's timing?
- What would it look like to patiently wait on the Lord in your current decision?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me the patience of Noah - to trust not only Your deliverance but Your timing. Help me wait on You rather than rushing ahead, knowing Your timing is always right.
